title: Subscription Audit Checklist: 30 Minutes Every Quarter
metaDescription: A 30-minute quarterly subscription audit for India. Gather app-store, UPI AutoPay and card charges, convert to monthly figures and cancel what you do not use.
h1: How do you audit your subscriptions in 30 minutes each quarter?
summary: A subscription audit is a 30-minute check every quarter: list every recurring charge from your statements and app-store accounts, convert each one to a monthly cost, then keep, cancel or downgrade it. Cancelling in the app or store does not always stop the charge, so the audit also covers UPI AutoPay mandates and card billing.

steps.name: Gather your sources (5 minutes)
steps.text: Open the last three months of your bank and card statements, the AutoPay or Mandates list in each UPI app you use, and the subscription pages in Google Play and the App Store. Check every Google Account and Apple Account you use, because a subscription can sit on a second account.

steps.name: List every recurring charge (5 minutes)
steps.text: Write each service, its amount, its billing cycle and its next renewal date in one list. Include weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly charges exactly as they appear.

steps.name: Convert everything to a monthly cost (5 minutes)
steps.text: Keep monthly prices as they are, divide quarterly prices by 3, divide yearly prices by 12, and multiply weekly prices by 52 then divide by 12. For example, a ₹1,999 yearly plan is about ₹167 a month. Add the results for your total monthly outflow on recurring services.

steps.name: Mark each item keep, cancel or downgrade (5 minutes)
steps.text: Keep anything you used in the last month or would genuinely miss. Mark the rest to cancel, or to switch to a cheaper plan if the service offers one.

steps.name: Cancel in the right place (5 minutes)
steps.text: For Google Play, open subscriptions in Google Play, select the subscription and tap Cancel subscription. On an iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, tap Subscriptions, tap the subscription and tap Cancel Subscription. For other services, use the cancel page in their own app or website.

steps.name: Stop UPI AutoPay mandates and card billing (3 minutes)
steps.text: Open the AutoPay or mandates section of each UPI app and revoke any mandate for a service you have cancelled. Menu names differ between apps and versions, so look for an option with a similar name. For card charges, note the merchant name and contact the merchant or your card issuer if the charge continues.

steps.name: Confirm each cancellation (2 minutes)
steps.text: Reopen each subscription and check that it shows as cancelled or expiring. On an iPhone, a missing Cancel button or an expiry message in red text means it has already been cancelled. Put the next review date in your calendar, and check the next statement for any charge from a cancelled service.

sections.heading: Why audit every quarter
paragraphs: A quarter is frequent enough to catch new renewals and short enough that you still remember what each charge is for. Yearly renewals and free trials that became paid plans are easy to miss in a monthly glance, so a quarterly check gives them a regular chance to be caught.
The audit only works if you write the list down. A charge you cannot see in one place is much easier to forget, especially when it comes through a different app or card.

sections.heading: Where recurring charges hide
paragraphs: App-store subscriptions are tied to the account that bought them. Google says that if you cannot find a subscription, it may be on a different account, so switch accounts and look again. Apple says that if you cannot find a receipt, the charge may come from another company, so check your bank or card statement to see who is billing you.
UPI AutoPay mandates sit in your UPI app, not in the service itself. Menu names vary between apps and versions, so look for an AutoPay or Mandates section in each app you use, not only your main one.
Card charges are the third source. A recurring merchant charge on a card statement may not appear in any app-store list, so compare the statement line by line with your list.

sections.heading: What to check after cancelling
paragraphs: Cancelling inside the service is a separate step from stopping the UPI mandate or card billing. On Google Play, cancelling stops the next renewal and you keep access for the time you have already paid. Uninstalling the app does not cancel it, so use the cancel option rather than deleting the app.
Check the mandate and the next card statement after you cancel, because a charge can keep coming through a route you did not cancel.

sections.heading: How tracking renewals in Essara helps
paragraphs: Keeping the audit list in Essara means it is not rebuilt from memory each quarter. Add each subscription and mandate with its billing cycle, and Essara shows the monthly and yearly cost along with upcoming renewals. It is manual, so the list is only as complete as the entries you make, and it does not connect to your bank account, UPI app or SMS.

faqs.q: How often should I audit my subscriptions?
faqs.a: Every quarter, which is what this checklist is designed for. Check sooner if you started a free trial or a yearly plan is due to renew soon.

faqs.q: What if I cancelled an app but the money still goes out?
faqs.a: Check whether the charge comes through a UPI mandate or a card merchant rather than the app store. Revoke the UPI mandate in the app that created it, or contact the card merchant or your card issuer. For app-store charges, check whether the subscription is on a different Google or Apple account.

faqs.q: Which subscriptions do people most often miss?
faqs.a: Yearly renewals, free trials that turned into paid plans, and services billed to a second Google or Apple account are easy to miss. Check those items on purpose during each audit rather than relying on memory.

faqs.q: What if I cannot find a subscription I am being charged for?
faqs.a: Search your email for a receipt from Apple or Google and check which account it was bought with. If it still does not appear, look at your bank or card statement to see which company is billing you, then contact that company.
